solves: Gives a product its main navigation in a horizontal bar: direct links and triggers that open a panel of grouped links, with the page the person is on marked by more than color.
use_when: For the main and stable sections of a product or site, always visible at the top.
A trigger when the section has inner pages; a top link when it goes straight to one page.
Two labeled groups in a panel when it puts together links of different kinds.
narrow when the items do not fit on one line: the bar turns into the Menu button, which opens the same items as a vertical list.
do_not_use_when: For actions on an object, such as delete: navigation goes to pages and does not change data; use nph-dropdown-menu.
As an application command bar (menubar): the piece is disclosure navigation, with no arrow-key menubar pattern.
To switch content on the same page: use tabs.
As side navigation with several levels: use the sidebar.
To hide the bar behind the Menu button when the items fit: menus hidden away reduce the discovery of the sections.

items.constraint: Property only. The top items of the bar, in order. A link item is { label, href } and a trigger item is { type: trigger, label, groups }, with an optional value that names it for active. Each group is { label, links } and each link is { title, href, description, icon, current, disabled }. label and title are required, already localized, on one line. href is required on every link, unless it is disabled, and takes http, https, mailto, tel or a relative address; any other protocol, javascript among them, in any spelling the browser reads as such, is refused. icon is optional, a core name of nph-icon. A list that is not a list or is empty, a trigger without groups, a group without links, two triggers with the same value or a link that breaks a rule above draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause. How many items, groups and links there are is composition.

narrow.constraint: It is the Figma value `estreita` of the property `largura`. On, the bar turns into the Menu button, which opens the same items as a vertical list; it needs menu-label, and without it the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development. The consumer chooses it, since the width is the page to know. Reflects so the consumer can style and check the state.

open.constraint: It is the Figma value `sim` of the property `aberto`. Wide, the panel of the active trigger is shown; narrow, the vertical list is shown. The piece turns it on and off, and the consumer may set it. Reflects. A bar that changes width while open closes.

active.constraint: The value of the trigger whose panel open shows. A trigger without a value has its index in items, as text. Empty or unknown: open shows the first trigger that is not disabled. A click on a trigger writes it.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the navigation landmark, already localized. It wins over the aria-label of the host. A bar with neither draws and warns once in development.

menu-label.constraint: The accessible name of the Menu button, already localized, such as Menu. Required when narrow, because the icon has no text. Not read when the bar is wide.

aria-label.constraint: The accessible name of the landmark when label is not given; label wins over it. It is read by a property whose attribute is aria-label, since a property called ariaLabel is the native ARIA reflection of the element. A bar with neither draws and warns once in development.

width.choose_when: Wide (the Figma `larga`) when the items fit on one line; narrow (`estreita`) when they do not, or on a narrow screen.

item.choose_when: A trigger (the Figma `gatilho`) when the section has inner pages; a top link (`link`) when it goes straight to one page.
do_not_combine_with: a link without href that is not disabled

icon.choose_when: An icon on a panel link (the Figma `ícone` yes) when it helps to recognize the page; without it (`não`) when the title is enough.
do_not_combine_with: an icon that does not belong to the core of nph-icon

top-rest.changes_for_user: The top item shows its text, with no background. A trigger carries the arrow.

top-hover.changes_for_user: The top item takes a background and the accent text. A trigger whose panel is open keeps this look.

top-focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo outside the item mark the focus; the item keeps the look of rest.

top-disabled.changes_for_user: The whole item loses opacity. It takes no hover and no focus.

top-current.changes_for_user: The text takes the current color and a bar under the item marks the page, so color is not the only signal. Focus adds the border and the halo.

link-rest.changes_for_user: The panel link shows its title, its optional description and its optional icon, with no background.

link-hover.changes_for_user: The link takes a background, the accent title and the accent icon.

link-focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo outside the link mark the focus.

link-disabled.changes_for_user: The whole link loses opacity. It takes no hover and no focus.

link-current.changes_for_user: The title and the icon take the current color and a bar at the start of the link marks the page; the icon is solid.

business_rules: A menu has one current page: at most one link is current. A trigger shows as current when its panel holds the current link.

A trigger opens its panel on click, Enter or Space. With the mouse, it opens after motion/hover-delay and closes the same time after the pointer leaves the trigger and the panel; the panel stays open while the pointer is over it. A click on a panel the pointer opened keeps it open.
Esc closes the panel and gives the focus back to its trigger. A click outside, and the focus leaving the bar, close it. Following a link closes it.
Disclosure navigation, not a menubar: Tab moves between the items and into the open panel, Enter and Space open and close. There are no arrow keys.
The wide panel hugs its content; the narrow panel and every panel link are navigation-menu/panel-width wide. Two groups sit side by side, with a vertical nph-separator between them.
The panel opens navigation-menu/panel-offset below its trigger, aligned to its start edge, and never leaves the window sideways.

narrow turns the bar into the Menu button, which opens the same items as a vertical list. Each trigger shows as a group, with its label as the group label, and the top links come together. The consumer chooses narrow; the piece does not measure itself.
The trigger arrow and the panel link icon are decorative. Light is the style of the icon, solid marks the current panel link.
The piece has no slot, no event and no featured card inside the panel, and only one level of panels.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the piece writes no word of its own.
domain_errors: An items that is not a list or is empty; an item or a link without label or title; a link without href that is not disabled, or with an unsafe protocol: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.
A trigger without groups, a group without links, or two triggers with the same value: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
An icon outside the core of nph-icon; more than one current link: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A narrow bar without menu-label: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A bar with no accessible name draws and warns once in development, because the name may arrive after the first render.

ai_hints: Use nph-navigation-menu for the main sections of a product, always visible at the top; for actions on an object use nph-dropdown-menu, for tabs use tabs, for side navigation use the sidebar.
Give items as a list: a link item has label and href, a trigger item has label and groups, and each group has links with title and href.
Use a trigger only when the section has inner pages; a section that goes straight to one page is a top link.
Mark the page the person is on with current on its link, only one in the whole menu; never mark the current page by color alone.
Group the panel links with a group label when they are of different kinds.
Give the bar a label, or an aria-label, because it is the accessible name of the navigation landmark.
Choose narrow when the items do not fit on one line, and then give menu-label; the piece does not measure itself.

accessibility.semantics: A nav, named. Each trigger is a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to its panel; the link of the current page carries aria-current page, and a trigger that holds it carries aria-current true. The panel is part of the page's Tab order, right after its trigger. The arrow and the link icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology. A panel link is named by its content, the title and the description. The Menu button is a native button with an accessible name and aria-expanded.
accessibility.accessible_name: The landmark: label, else the aria-label of the host. A trigger: its label. A link: its content, the title and the optional description. The Menu button: menu-label, because its icon has no text.
keyboard: Tab moves between the top items and, when a panel is open, through its links, which come right after their trigger.
Enter and Space on a trigger open or close its panel; Enter follows a link.
Esc closes the open panel and gives the focus back to its trigger, or to the Menu button.
There are no arrow keys: this is disclosure navigation, not a menubar.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only, on the top item, the panel link and the Menu button: a border of border/width in focus/border and a halo in focus/halo outside the box, without changing its size. The border carries the focus; the halo is reinforcement. A disabled item takes no focus.
accessibility.contrast: The text of the top items and of the panel links, the description and the icons pass the required WCAG level over the background in both themes. The indicator and the focus border, in the primary color, have at least 3:1 against the background in both schemes.
accessibility.color_alternative: The current page is told apart without color: the indicator comes with the current text color (WCAG 1.4.1). The open trigger shows its panel and the hover background.

invalid_combinations: narrow without menu-label — the Menu button has an icon and no text.
A trigger without groups or a group without links — the panel would be empty.
More than one current link — a menu has one current page.
A link without href that is not disabled, or with an unsafe protocol.
An icon outside the core of nph-icon.
Two triggers with the same value.

parents: the top of the page, in the header of a product or site

anti_patterns: Using the menu for actions on an object, such as delete.
Marking the current page by color alone.
Hiding the bar behind the Menu button when the items fit.
Opening a trigger for a section that has no inner pages.
Putting a featured card or a second level of panels inside the panel.
Leaving the bar without a label or an aria-label.
